# Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself, and What a Falling Score Actually Measures

Wenhui Chen ^(†)^(†)thanks: mc35092@um.edu.mo Affiliation: University of
Macau    Jianlin Chen ^(†)^(†)thanks: 202330450231@mail.scut.edu.cn
Affiliation: South China University of Technology    Ziyao Lin
^(†)^(†)thanks: mc35081@um.edu.mo Affiliation: University of Macau   
Chi Man Vong ^(†)^(†)thanks: Corresponding author. cmvong@um.edu.mo
Affiliation: University of Macau

###### Abstract

An agent that writes its conclusions into a store it later retrieves
from closes a loop, and the contamination has been reported as a one-way
process \[[76](#bib.bib10), [66](#bib.bib9), [73](#bib.bib23)\]. Taking
that loop to the infinite-tenure limit against an append-only store
gives a different picture. Because writing never deletes, the reachable
state space has a hard upper edge at $`(n{-}1)/n`$, so the outcome is a
choice between two edges rather than a decay: the upper mode is not an
attractor but a wall the store builds itself. At $`f_{0}{=}0.9`$ the
interval between the two modes holds $`3.6\%`$ of $`220`$ runs where a
uniform spread would put $`20.6\%`$, and is strictly empty on the first
$`15`$. Four of seven captured runs finish within two records of the
computed ceiling $`0.9938`$. Against a criterion frozen beforehand, the
pooled mean describes $`8.2\%`$ of the runs it summarises and the median
$`68.2\%`$. A per-model average of this process is a statistic with no
referent.

Everything the model contributes is carried by one measured primitive
with no fitted parameter, the copy function $`\gamma(\varphi)`$, and it
survives the move to real facts. Replacing the synthetic world by $`36`$
Wikidata facts spanning the full range of measured prior knowledge
leaves the threshold intact:
$`\mathrm{sign}(\hat{\gamma}-\gamma_{\rm crit})`$, with
$`\gamma_{\rm crit}=1/k`$ at $`r{=}0,w{=}1`$, predicts the direction of
drift on $`353`$ of $`360`$ real-fact runs, against $`39`$ of $`40`$
synthetic runs in the same batch; the denominators differ ninefold, so
the reading is that the threshold survives, not that the rates differ.
The copy probability under a unanimous false store falls from $`0.711`$
to $`0.411`$ across prior terciles, and the synthetic world sits
$`0.300`$ above the real curve’s low-prior end, so it bounds the risk
rather than instantiating it. Nor does the empty interval come from the
answer space: a state-independent reader on the identical urn puts
$`113`$ of $`300`$ runs inside it, so what empties it is the copy
probability rising with the number of false records retrieved. Scale
does not rescue the store: at frontier scale capture is $`0.850`$
pooled, with claude-sonnet-4.5 captured on $`20`$ of $`20`$ seeds,
against a registered prediction of ours of $`{<}0.5`$.

We then attack the result on the axes a reader will, and report the
disagreement rather than the arm that suits us. Whether a store holding
_many_ distinct falsehoods still has an empty interval is answered
differently by our two arms: on the synthetic world the
highest-scattering model has $`0`$ of $`44`$ runs inside it, while on
the $`36`$ Wikidata facts, where the planted falsehood is another real
capital, the runs whose store went multi-valued have $`6.4\times`$ the
interval occupancy of those that did not. That relocates the open
question from how many falsehoods a store holds to how _distinguishable_
they are. The empty interval survives at $`f_{0}\in\{0.1,0.3,0.5\}`$,
and $`f_{0}{=}0.9`$ is not the adversarial extreme: capture peaks at
$`f_{0}{=}0.5`$. Of four interventions with criteria frozen first,
timing dominates fraction at matched budget, a consistency gate drives
every model to $`0.993`$ by helping the false majority, and provenance
marking moves nothing unless the mark correlates with truth. Two
registered arms test the apparatus itself: an embedding ranking moves
capture by $`0.500`$, so the uniform assumption is not innocuous and
every threshold here is scoped to it by name; and a sweep of the
fraction of frozen retrieval slots reproduces both endpoints exactly
while refuting the variance account we proposed for them. One
methodological result reaches past this paper: the resampling unit is
the _seed_, at a design effect of $`3.75`$ on a pooled level and
$`1.14`$–$`1.47`$ on a paired within-seed contrast measured at $`44`$
seeds. Every verdict here stands under it, including the four
interventions’, under a $`44`$-seed control that moves their control’s
capture rate by up to $`0.68`$. It also reaches the two per-model
orderings, which move in opposite directions: claim 4, that the early
copy rate orders capture rate, falls from Spearman $`+0.98`$ at three
seeds to $`+0.31`$ to $`+0.80`$ at forty-four, while claim 2’s ordering,
$`+0.82`$ “with one adjacent inversion” at three seeds, is exact at
forty-four ($`\rho=+1.00`$, $`p=0.017`$). The $`1/n`$ account of this
paper’s own timescale is vacuous over the first $`49`$ of $`150`$ steps
while the decision is measured at $`t{=}2`$
(Prop. [4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (Per-step bound). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
All $`87`$ graded rows are in
Appendix [W](#A23 "Appendix W The scorecard, every graded row ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"),
$`37`$ graded withdrawn, failed, self-correcting, undecidable or an
acknowledged limit, against $`50`$ that are not.

## 1 Introduction

An agent that writes notes to itself and later reads them has closed a
loop: its output becomes its input. Wrong entries are retrieved,
reinforced and rewritten, and the store drifts with no external source
of error. This is the deployment-time analogue of training on generated
data \[[60](#bib.bib2), [1](#bib.bib3)\], with one difference that
changes the mathematics: the store is _append-only_, so nothing is
removed, only diluted. The failure is documented at the level of
deployed agents \[[66](#bib.bib9), [76](#bib.bib10), [8](#bib.bib15)\],
and the systems in which it arises are ordinary: agents that write
reflections or episodic summaries back into a retrieved store
\[[51](#bib.bib64), [59](#bib.bib65), [49](#bib.bib63)\] on top of the
standard retrieve-then-generate pipeline \[[37](#bib.bib66)\]. What is
missing is a measurement of the _dynamics_: what the loop converges to,
and which of its knobs the outcome is a function of.

Sending the loop to infinity with that constraint pinned organises the
paper. Let $`f`$ be the false share of the store and $`n`$ the number of
records retrieved per step. The mean field is
$`\dot{f}=\bigl(G_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)-f\bigr)/n`$, and because writing
never deletes, the reachable state space has a hard upper edge at
$`(n{-}1)/n`$, which for our apparatus is $`0.9938`$. Two boundaries
therefore come from the limit rather than from the literature: what the
store can hold, and what a bounded grounding budget $`R`$ can hold it
to, $`f_{\max}(R)=(n_{\mathrm{false},0}+Tw)/(n_{0}+Tw+R)`$. The second
is the useful one: the governing quantity is then a budget rather than a
fixed _fraction_ of verified data, and the same budget spent early or
late gives different outcomes. _That is where our setting and the
generational one come apart._ The accumulate-versus-replace results
\[[25](#bib.bib6), [60](#bib.bib2)\] and the analytical line
\[[16](#bib.bib7), [24](#bib.bib5)\] are stated in terms of the
_proportion_ of real data, since there real data is present every round
and re-usable without limit, so no scheduling question arises. The
closest budgeted analogue is the data-constrained regime, where a fixed
corpus is re-used a bounded number of times \[[46](#bib.bib46)\] and
allocation under a fixed budget is the object \[[36](#bib.bib43),
[30](#bib.bib44)\]; even there the budget buys repetition rather than
placement in time. Under a bounded per-tenure budget the placement
question does arise, and
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures that it dominates the proportion.

##### Contributions.

\(i\) The outcome distribution is _bimodal_ rather than a decaying mean,
and one measured primitive with no fitted parameter, the copy function
$`\gamma(\varphi)`$, says which way a model goes
(§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
It _transports_, and the condition under which it does is itself a
result: measured at the resolution it must predict at, $`\gamma`$
calibrated on three topics carries to forty-four; measured coarser it
fails one-sidedly, which fixes the resolution
(§[4.1.5](#S4.SS1.SSS5 "4.1.5 Claim 2 out of sample, at a 14× harder bar ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
Against a criterion frozen first, the pooled mean describes $`8.2\%`$ of
the runs it summarises and the median $`68.2\%`$, so the defect is in
that statistic and not in summarising. (ii) A falling exact-match score
on a contaminated store measures loss of determinism, not of
information: pass@8 minus pass@1 is $`+0.383`$ on stores from which
nothing was removed, so a score reads $`C\cdot s`$, capability times
commitment
(§[4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 What a falling score measures ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
(iii) Four interventions with criteria frozen before their data, and the
design rule they yield: timing dominates fraction at matched budget, so
_when_ a grounding budget is spent matters more than how much of it
there is; a consistency admission gate helps the false majority, the
record-level analogue of the adversarial-majority failure [Liu et al.
\[41\]](#bib.bib24) report between agents; and provenance marking
\[[75](#bib.bib17), [72](#bib.bib18)\] moves outcomes only when the mark
correlates with truth
(§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
(iv) Three axes of our own proposing, taken to destruction against
pre-registrations we wrote first
(§[4.7](#S4.SS7 "4.7 Three withdrawn axes ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
(v) A methodological result that reaches past this paper: the resampling
unit is the _seed_, whose variance share reads $`2.0\%`$ at three seeds
and $`68.8\%`$ at nine, a design effect of $`3.75`$, so each seed
carries $`1.33`$ runs of information however many models are run
(§[L](#A12 "Appendix L Unresolvability from the boundary structure ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
(vi) That result applied to every row it had not reached, which makes
the verdicts here load-bearing: it separates cleanly into a factor of
$`3.56`$–$`3.66`$ on pooled _levels_ and $`1.14`$–$`1.47`$ on paired
_contrasts_, both measured at $`44`$ seeds, so the four interventions’
criteria stand, one is regraded underpowered for missing its own bar on
one of its three seeds, claim 2’s ordering is exact and claim 4’s does
not survive
(§[4.8](#S4.SS8 "4.8 The falsifier on the unreached rows ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
(vii) The scope of claim 1, measured rather than argued: the empty
interval is not a consequence of a two-valued answer space, and the
regime it holds in has a boundary in how far a store’s falsehoods
scatter
(§[4.1.1](#S4.SS1.SSS1 "4.1.1 Two objections to the empty interval ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
[Bean et al. \[4\]](#bib.bib31) report that only $`16\%`$ of $`445`$
benchmarks use uncertainty estimates; this paper is in the $`16\%`$ and
§[L](#A12 "Appendix L Unresolvability from the boundary structure ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
is why that was not sufficient, which is the same gap the
evaluation-precision line attacks from the item side \[[56](#bib.bib33),
[31](#bib.bib34), [47](#bib.bib35)\].

Every registered claim, its frozen criterion and its grade are in

Where a criterion floored, the apparatus failure is reported rather than

What we do not claim. Not priority: that an agent’s own outputs degrade
its later behaviour is prior work, named in

_where_ the boundary between the two outcomes sits. Not transfer to
generational retraining. Not incidence in deployed stores; our worlds
are synthetic because traceability requires it. No longer retrieval in
general:
§[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 The retrieval rule’s own falsifier ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")

number here is a statement about uniform-without-replacement.

## 2 Related work

We ask one question of each neighbouring result: what must be true for
its conclusion to hold, and does our apparatus put that assumption under
strain? A result that survives is one we depend on. A result that does
not is not thereby wrong; its scope can now be stated more narrowly than
its authors could, because we ran a limit they had no reason to run.
Table [1](#S2.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 2 Related work ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
states row by row what each neighbour establishes and what is added
here.

| Prior work                                                                         | What it establishes                                                                    | What is added here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Self-Confirmation Trap \[[76](#bib.bib10)\]                                        | the closed loop named: own trajectories written to memory and reused                   | the outcome is bimodal rather than cumulative, and one primitive predicts which branch                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| State contamination \[[66](#bib.bib9)\]                                            | unsafe content survives summarisation below detector thresholds                        | a different failure axis; no dynamics, no copy probability there                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Admission control \[[73](#bib.bib23)\]                                             | write-time gating on self-consistency reduces contamination                            | the same gate has a regime where it erases the model’s own cleaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Majority aggregation traps \[[41](#bib.bib24), [29](#bib.bib25)\]                  | one-shot majority over samples locks in correlated error                               | the write side over tenure, where the gate decouples composition from reader quality                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Accumulate vs. replace \[[25](#bib.bib6), [16](#bib.bib7)\]                        | accumulating real with synthetic data avoids collapse                                  | a _budgeted_ grounding event, where schedule dominates at fixed fraction                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Exact-match and pass@$`k`$ critiques                                               | strict matching understates capability; pass^(k) separates capability from reliability | an intervention that conserves $`C`$ while moving $`s`$                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Threat amplification in self-evolving systems \[[39](#bib.bib11), [1](#bib.bib3)\] | a component’s failure is amplified by the loop that reuses its output                  | the amplification as one number with a fixed point, whose attractor is ([2](#S3.E2 "In Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")) rather than a divergence |
| State-conditioned memory \[[18](#bib.bib12)\]                                      | compiling a policy against state beats injecting retrieved text                        | the ceiling binds what the store _contains_, so it binds whatever the compiler reads                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 1: Nearest prior work. Every row is a phenomenon this paper does
_not_ claim to have discovered.

##### Model collapse assumes the damage is summarised by a decaying statistic.

Training a generative model on its predecessor’s output degrades it
\[[60](#bib.bib2), [1](#bib.bib3), [7](#bib.bib56)\], costing tail
coverage \[[19](#bib.bib52), [57](#bib.bib54)\] and output diversity
\[[27](#bib.bib55)\]; the analytical line \[[16](#bib.bib7),
[24](#bib.bib5), [5](#bib.bib53)\] derives when it is bounded, and
collapse is avoidable if data accumulates rather than replaces
\[[25](#bib.bib6)\] or if a correction function stabilises the loop
\[[26](#bib.bib4)\]. Each result is a trajectory of a summary statistic
across generations, which needs the per-run outcome distribution to be
unimodal enough for its mean to denote something.
§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures the same loop at fixed tenure and finds otherwise: at
$`f_{0}{=}0.9`$ runs end at the two edges of the state space and the
interval between them holds $`3.6\%`$ of $`220`$ runs against a uniform
baseline of $`20.6\%`$. The step from that to a claim about summary
statistics is itself a claim, so we registered and measured it
(P-T1-M1–M4; no API cost): the pooled mean describes $`8.2\%`$ of what
it summarises, the median $`68.2\%`$, against $`74.5\%`$ for the best
single centre at that width
(Appendix [A](#A1 "Appendix A E-mean: a single centre ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
_This distribution summarises perfectly well; it is the mean that does
not_, and the wider criticism is unsupported by our own data. Two
structural differences keep the settings apart, so the generational
results are not wrong in their own: retraining averages over a corpus
while an agent’s read samples $`k`$ of $`n`$ records, so the variance
driving our bimodality is averaged away there by construction; and real
data is present every round and reusable without limit, the $`R\to T`$
corner in which our schedule effect vanishes.

##### Feedback-loop results outside language modelling assume the loop is closed through the world.

A deployed predictor that shapes the data it is later trained on is the
subject of performative prediction \[[54](#bib.bib58)\], of runaway
feedback in predictive policing \[[22](#bib.bib59)\], of degenerate
feedback in recommenders \[[34](#bib.bib60)\] and of model-driven
amplification of dataset bias \[[61](#bib.bib57)\]. Those loops close
through an environment whose response is exogenous: the analysis turns
on how the world reacts to the deployed model. Our loop closes inside
one process, with no environment and no second agent, so none of that
machinery applies and what is left is the reading behaviour of a single
model against records it wrote itself. The lesson we keep is theirs: the
fixed point of the loop, not the quality of any single prediction, is
the object to analyse.

##### Knowledge conflict fixes the contradiction and varies the model; we let the loop generate it.

Whether a model follows a context that contradicts what it has memorised
is measured directly by the knowledge-conflict line: entity substitution
in QA \[[43](#bib.bib47)\], elicited parametric memory against
constructed counter-memory \[[68](#bib.bib48)\], and the parametric
baseline those studies contend with \[[55](#bib.bib51)\]. Which side
wins is known to depend on how well the fact is represented in
pretraining \[[44](#bib.bib49), [35](#bib.bib50)\]. Our
$`\gamma(\varphi)`$ is that measurement made _in situ_: the conflicting
evidence is produced by the agent’s own earlier writes rather than
authored by an experimenter, its strength is the retrieved fraction
$`\varphi`$ rather than a binary condition, and it is measured on the
same runs whose trajectories it must predict.
§[4.6](#S4.SS6 "4.6 The synthetic world on a real axis ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
puts the parametric axis those papers vary, our $`p_{0}`$, on the same
plot as the loop, and finds $`\gamma(1)`$ falling from $`0.711`$ to
$`0.411`$ across prior terciles while the drift threshold does not move.

##### Agent-memory contamination assumes contamination is a quantity to be reduced.

A second line studies the same failure in the store rather than the
weights: contamination surviving summarisation into agent state
\[[66](#bib.bib9)\], the self-confirmation trap \[[76](#bib.bib10)\],
the best models near $`55\%`$ at noticing an invalidated memory
\[[8](#bib.bib15)\], the memory-update gap scaling with conversation
length \[[52](#bib.bib14)\], retrieval accuracy falling log-linearly
under proactive interference \[[64](#bib.bib13)\], and three surveys
\[[17](#bib.bib16), [32](#bib.bib75), [21](#bib.bib76)\], the last of
which organises the field by the write–manage–read cycle this apparatus
closes. The shared move treats contamination as a level to drive down,
which assumes the final level is a monotone function of the level along
the way.
§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures that it is not: the sign of the trajectory is fixed in the
first few steps and the same $`f_{0}`$ produces both outcomes, so an
intervention’s value is set by when it lands rather than by how much it
removes.

##### The closest result to ours assumes the store is _not_ append-only, which is exactly the assumption we pin.

[Yang et al. \[69\]](#bib.bib72) characterise the steady-state occupancy
of erroneous coordinates in a self-evolving agent memory, under a
coordinate-transition model over a _fixed_ coordinate set whose contents
are updated or replaced, and measure it on ALFWorld and
LifelongAgentBench. That is the same object as our $`f`$ and the same
limit, taken under the opposite structural assumption: replacement gives
an ergodic chain with a stationary distribution, so a steady-state
occupancy exists and is the natural answer. Append-only forbids
replacement, which puts a hard edge at $`(n{-}1)/n`$
(Prop. [1](#Thmproposition1 "Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")),
removes the stationary distribution, and leaves a _choice between edges_
rather than an occupancy to converge to. The two results do not compete
and neither transfers: our
Prop. [1](#Thmproposition1 "Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
is vacuous the moment a record can be overwritten, and a stationary
occupancy is undefined in our setting. This is the boundary
§[5.2](#S5.SS2 "5.2 Limitations ‣ 5 Discussion ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")(i)
declared as a hole in our own coverage, better stated as a division of
labour with a measured neighbour, with one asymmetry we owe: their
regime is the deployed one, ours the one an append-only design produces.

##### Memory poisoning assumes an adversary, and our store has none.

Knowledge-base corruption at low poison rates \[[14](#bib.bib20)\],
adversarial passages injected into a retrieval corpus
\[[74](#bib.bib62), [77](#bib.bib61)\], query-only injection
\[[20](#bib.bib21)\] and sentries against high injection rates
\[[63](#bib.bib22)\] are all organised around locating an injected item.
Our apparatus removes the attacker: every false record after step $`0`$
is written by the agent itself, in good faith, from what it read, so a
detector trained to find injected content has no positive class here and
the store still reaches $`0.99`$ false. Contamination needs no
adversary, and a defence keyed to one does not bound it.

##### Provenance assumes the mark carries information about truth.

Tiered and watermarked memories \[[75](#bib.bib17), [72](#bib.bib18)\]
and the tracing survey \[[67](#bib.bib19)\] make each record’s origin
recoverable so a reader can discount derived records.
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
registers and measures that prediction: marking moves outcomes only when
the mark correlates with truth, and in our loop it does not, the agent’s
own writes being as often right as its reads permit.

##### Consistency and majority reads assume the majority is more often right.

Admission on repeated sampling \[[73](#bib.bib23)\], which inherits the
majority rule from self-consistency decoding \[[65](#bib.bib67)\],
majority voting failing under corrupted majorities \[[41](#bib.bib24)\]
and the minority correct in roughly one disagreement in four
\[[29](#bib.bib25)\] all read the majority as evidence.
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures a majority admission gate inside our loop and finds it erases
model differences by making every model worse alike: once the store is
majority-false, the gate admits exactly the falsehood and rejects the
correction. [Liu et al. \[41\]](#bib.bib24) anticipate this among agents
in a debate; we measure it among records in a store, where the
adversarial majority is the reader’s own past. Two deployed admission
controls are richer than ours and are the right comparison. [Zhang et
al. \[71\]](#bib.bib74) admit on five retention factors (future utility,
factual confidence, semantic novelty, temporal recency and a
content-type prior), so agreement with the incumbent store is one signal
of five rather than the whole rule. [Ha et al. \[28\]](#bib.bib73) do
what our own mechanism predicts would help: they _type_ memories by
functional role and keep the types separate at storage and at retrieval,
changing the gate’s reference class instead of filtering within it, and
the reference class is where we locate the harm. We do not claim our
result transfers to either, and a harmful regime in the weakest gate is
not “conservative evidence about stronger versions”: that inference
needs monotonicity in gate strength, which we have not tested
(§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).

##### The benchmarks measure retrieval; the object here is the loop.

BEAM \[[62](#bib.bib26)\], STATE-Bench \[[45](#bib.bib29)\], RECON
\[[2](#bib.bib28)\] and the precision-aware line \[[23](#bib.bib27)\]
evaluate what an agent can retrieve from a memory it is given, and [Liu
et al. \[40\]](#bib.bib30) and [Huang et al. \[33\]](#bib.bib8) address
the adjacent problem that retrieval corpora are increasingly
model-generated. All hold the store fixed and vary the reader; we hold
the reader fixed and let the store be written by it, making its
composition endogenous rather than a condition of the experiment.
§[4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 What a falling score measures ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
shows a system can score well on the first design and fail the second.
Figure [3](#S3.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
is the loop this paper runs and the place each claim attaches to it.

## 3 The synthetic apparatus

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 3: The apparatus, and where the claims attach. One move (retrieve
$`k`$ of $`n`$, answer, append one record), run for $`T`$ steps with
$`R`$ of them grounded. Fixing $`R`$ and sending $`T`$ to infinity makes
two boundaries visible, and the alternative to the ceiling is zero
rather than a lower plateau. Claim 1 is that runs end at one boundary or
the other; claim 2 that $`\gamma`$ alone says which; claim 3 that the
choice is made in the first few steps.

|                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| world              | one tracked topic: a generated entity (Baldrix Holdings) with a generated numeric attribute (68.91M). The false value is a _one-digit_ corruption: plausible, never equal, unreachable by guessing |
| store at $`t{=}0`$ | $`n_{0}{=}10`$ records, $`n_{\mathrm{false}}\in\{1,9\}`$ of them asserting the corruption, giving $`f_{0}\in\{0.1,0.9\}`$                                                                          |
| each step          | retrieve $`k{=}8`$ records uniformly from the topic; ask the plain question a deployed assistant would be asked; append the answer                                                                 |
| prompt             | never states the truth, never warns of error, so $`\gamma`$ measures ordinary behaviour rather than a response to a warning                                                                        |
| tenure             | $`150`$ steps, growing the store from $`11`$ to $`161`$ records: a $`15\times`$ range in $`n`$, which is what makes the $`1/n`$ term visible within one run                                        |
| models             | five, three seeds, temperature $`0`$                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 2: The protocol. Every arm is this loop with one thing changed.

##### Why the world is generated.

Traceability requires it: a propagated error is attributable only if the
truth is known by construction, and with a real corpus a wrong answer is
indistinguishable from a wrong prior
(Table [2](#S3.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
The same reasoning drives leakage-free benchmark generation
\[[40](#bib.bib30)\] and the detection of model-generated text inside a
retrieval corpus \[[33](#bib.bib8)\]; we generate the world because we
need not only that the answer is parametrically unavailable but that
every false record’s _provenance within the run_ is recoverable. The
cost is
§[5.2](#S5.SS2 "5.2 Limitations ‣ 5 Discussion ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")(vii).

##### Why retrieval is uniform.

Uniform-without-replacement within the topic is the assumption
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
makes, so the first experiment tests the predicted dynamics rather than
their interaction with an embedding model’s idiosyncrasies. It is also
what most separates this apparatus from the memory benchmarks
\[[62](#bib.bib26), [45](#bib.bib29), [2](#bib.bib28),
[23](#bib.bib27)\], which hold the store fixed and vary the reader. The
choice carries a falsifier: swapping in an embedding retriever changes
which records compete, and if the behaviour moves, that displacement is
the finding rather than a nuisance.
§[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 The retrieval rule’s own falsifier ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
fires it, and the behaviour moves, by $`-0.500`$ at $`f_{0}=0.1`$ and
$`+0.067`$ at $`f_{0}=0.9`$.

##### How $`\gamma`$ is measured, and why it is not fitted.

At every step the number $`j`$ of retrieved records asserting a false
value is logged with whether the answer was the truth, and pooling over
steps gives $`\gamma(j/k)`$ directly, from the same runs whose
trajectories are being predicted. The curve is an observation of reading
behaviour rather than a parameter tuned to fit a trajectory, and
§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
puts it back into the loop in place of the model, the only sense in
which “$`\gamma`$ is enough” can be checked rather than asserted.

###### Definition 1 (The copy function).

$`\gamma(\varphi)`$ is the probability that the agent asserts a false
value when a fraction $`\varphi`$ of the $`k`$ retrieved records assert
it. With $`f`$ the false share of the store,
$`\varphi\sim\mathrm{Bin}(k,f)/k`$, so the per-step assertion
probability is
$`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)=\mathbb{E}_{\varphi}[\gamma(\varphi)]`$ and,
with one write per step,

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

       ``` math
       \dot{f}\;=\;\frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)-f}{n}.
       ```                                                |     | (1) |

Equation ([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
licenses a per-step statement and this paper’s empirical content is not
carried by it.
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
looks like the model and is not. Its apparent content is the
denominator, a restoring force divided by a store that grows without
bound, and we drew three readings from that denominator, of which _one
survives_. The sign of $`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)-f`$ gives the
_direction_ of drift, which a mean-field reading would use to predict
the outcome;
§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures that four of five models drift downward at $`f_{0}`$ and are
captured anyway, so the direction is real and does not locate the
boundary. We read the $`1/n`$ as deciding _how long_ the outcome stays
open;
Prop. [4](#Thmproposition4 "Proposition 4 (Per-step bound). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
refutes that, the bound being vacuous over exactly the interval in which
the outcome is decided. We read the same $`1/n`$ as fixing the _spread_
of outcomes;
§[4.1.6](#S4.SS1.SSS6 "4.1.6 What the limit says about the two outcomes ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")’s
$`n_{0}`$ sweep refutes it at $`1.07\times`$ against a required
$`2.83\times`$. What is left is the per-step statement
([5](#S3.E5 "In Proposition 4 (Per-step bound). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
and the ceiling
([2](#S3.E2 "In Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")),
both exact, both about what the store _can_ hold. The empirical content
of this paper is carried by $`\gamma`$: the existence of two outcomes,
which model goes which way, and the ordering are measurements of
$`\gamma(\varphi)`$ put back into the loop
(§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"),
§[4.1.5](#S4.SS1.SSS5 "4.1.5 Claim 2 out of sample, at a 14× harder bar ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")),
none of it derived from
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
A reader who deletes
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
loses the notation and none of the results.

### 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions

Each of the following is elementary, and each is here rather than beside
the measurement it governs because each _constrains what a criterion may
say_. Two of this paper’s frozen criteria failed for reasons derivable
from these statements before their data existed
(§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"),
§[L](#A12 "Appendix L Unresolvability from the boundary structure ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")),
which is the argument for stating them up front. Proofs are in
Appendix [F](#A6 "Appendix F Proofs ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures").

###### Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling).

Let the store hold $`n(t)`$ records at step $`t`$, of which
$`n_{\mathrm{false}}(t)`$ are false, and let no record ever be removed.
Then the $`n_{0}-n_{\mathrm{false}}(0)`$ truth records present at
$`t{=}0`$ are present at every later step, so the false share obeys

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
f(t)\;=\;\frac{n_{\mathrm{false}}(t)}{n(t)}\;\leq\;\frac{n(t)-\bigl(n_{0}-n_{\mathrm{false}}(0)\bigr)}{n(t)}\;<\;1\qquad\text{for all finite }t,
``` |  | (2) |

with equality exactly when every write after $`t{=}0`$ is false. Under a
grounding budget of $`R`$ steps, $`R`$ of the writes are true by
construction, giving the per-run bound
$`f_{\max}(R)=(n_{\mathrm{false}}(0)+W)/(n_{0}+W+R)`$ where $`W`$ is the
number of ungrounded writes the run actually made.

$`f_{\max}(R)`$ moves with the budget, so any criterion stated as an
absolute threshold on $`f`$ silently becomes a different criterion at
each $`R`$.
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
records a criterion of ours that failed by it.

###### Proposition 2 (Log-dilution).

A grounded write at step $`t`$ multiplies $`f`$ by $`n/(n{+}1)`$ with
$`n=n_{0}+t`$, so $`R`$ grounded writes placed at steps
$`t_{1}\ldots t_{R}`$ multiply $`f`$ by
$`\prod_{i}(n_{0}{+}t_{i})/(n_{0}{+}t_{i}{+}1)`$, i.e. deliver a total
log-dilution

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
L\;=\;\sum_{i=1}^{R}\frac{1}{n_{0}+t_{i}}\;+\;O\!\left(\sum_{i}(n_{0}+t_{i})^{-2}\right),\qquad\begin{aligned} L_{\mathrm{front}}&\approx\ln\!\frac{n_{0}{+}R}{n_{0}},\\
L_{\mathrm{unif}}&\approx\frac{R}{T}\ln\!\frac{n_{0}{+}T}{n_{0}},\\
L_{\mathrm{back}}&\approx\ln\!\frac{n_{0}{+}T}{n_{0}{+}T{-}R},\end{aligned}
``` |  | (3) |

for the three schedules that place the $`R`$ writes first, evenly, and
last. The three are strictly ordered
$`L_{\mathrm{front}}>L_{\mathrm{unif}}>L_{\mathrm{back}}`$ for every
$`0<R<T`$, with no free parameter.

The ordering is parameter-free and is the schedule axis’s claim; the
magnitudes are not, since a bounded observable must compress an
unbounded one.

###### Proposition 3 (Resolution at $`s`$ seeds).

If $`f_{\mathrm{end}}`$ is two-valued with choice probability $`p`$,
then a per-model mean over $`s`$ seeds has

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{se}(\hat{p})\;=\;\sqrt{p(1-p)/s}\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;\mathrm{se}\approx 0.29\text{ at }s{=}3,\qquad 0.19\text{ at }s{=}7,
``` |  | (4) |

and for a quantity pooled over $`m`$ models sharing the same $`s`$
seeds, with intraclass correlation $`\rho`$ over seeds, the effective
sample size is $`sm/\bigl(1+(m{-}1)\rho\bigr)`$.

Two scopings the second half needs, both measured rather than assumed.
It is a statement about a pooled *level*; a within-seed *contrast*
cancels the seed effect and carries a design effect near one, measured
at $`1.14`$–$`1.47`$ against the level’s $`3.56`$–$`3.66`$ on the same
$`44`$-seed runs
(§[4.8](#S4.SS8 "4.8 The falsifier on the unreached rows ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
It writes one $`\rho`$ for $`m`$ models: measured pair by pair at $`44`$
seeds, $`\rho`$ runs $`+0.18`$ to $`+0.99`$, so the implied design
effect runs $`1.73`$–$`4.95`$ and the single figure this paper quotes is
a mean over heterogeneous pairs. Every correction’s direction is
unchanged and the mean $`\rho`$ is $`+0.53`$ to $`+0.65`$; what is not
safe is reading $`3.75`$ as a per-pair constant, and
§[L](#A12 "Appendix L Unresolvability from the boundary structure ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
carries the range.

###### Proposition 4 (Per-step bound).

Each step appends exactly one record, so

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bigl|f(t{+}1)-f(t)\bigr|\;\leq\;\frac{1}{n_{0}+t+1},\qquad\sum_{s=t}^{T-1}\frac{1}{n_{0}+s+1}\;=\;\log\frac{n_{0}+T}{n_{0}+t}+O(n_{0}^{-1}).
``` |  | (5) |

The cumulative bound is therefore *logarithmic* in the remaining tenure,
and it constrains nothing until it falls below $`1`$. At this paper’s
apparatus ($`n_{0}=10`$, $`T=150`$) that happens at $`t=49`$: for the
first $`49`$ steps
([5](#S3.E5 "In Proposition 4 (Per-step bound). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
permits $`f`$ to reach either endpoint from anywhere.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The second half of
Prop. [3](#Thmproposition3 "Proposition 3 (Resolution at 𝑠 seeds). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
is the one that caught us.
([4](#S3.E4 "In Proposition 3 (Resolution at 𝑠 seeds). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
is *per model*; the design-effect factor $`1+(m{-}1)\rho`$ applies to
everything pooled across models, which is most of what this paper
reports.
§[L](#A12 "Appendix L Unresolvability from the boundary structure ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures $`\rho`$ and gets $`3.75`$ at nine seeds, so $`45`$ runs carry
the information of $`12`$;
§[4.8](#S4.SS8 "4.8 The falsifier on the unreached rows ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
measures it again at forty-four and separates the case it does and does
not apply to.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

#### 4.1.1 Two objections to the empty interval

The apparatus plants one false value and corrupts one digit of it, so
the store’s realised answer space is small and a reader is entitled to
ask whether the empty interval is a fact about a self-writing loop or
arithmetic on a two-valued outcome. The question has two halves with
different answers, both settled without an API call.

##### A two-valued answer space does not empty the interval.

By construction
$`f_{\mathrm{end}}=(n_{\mathrm{false},0}+\#\{\text{false writes}\})/(n_{0}+T)`$,
so a reader whose copy probability does not depend on the store lands
where that constant puts it, in the interior. Running the identical urn
with the model replaced by a coin of fixed bias puts $`113`$ of $`300`$
runs inside the dead band at $`p{=}0.3`$ and $`82`$ of $`300`$ at
$`p{=}0.5`$
(Table [38](#A18.T38 "Table 38 ‣ The arithmetic half: a two-valued space does not empty the interval. ‣ Appendix R The answer space and the empty interval ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
*What empties the interval is the copy probability rising with the
number of false records retrieved*, a property of the reader and the
object $`\gamma(j)`$ measures. The two-valued space is not sufficient,
so it is not the explanation.

##### The premise is not uniformly true either, and our two arms disagree about what follows.

E-bimodal2’s runs log, step by step, whether each write was the truth,
the planted falsehood or a value the store had not seen. Writing $`q`$
for the share of non-truth writes that took a fresh value, the median
run has $`q{=}0`$, while qwen3-8b has a median of $`43`$ novel-value
*writes* in $`150`$ steps, $`q=0.33`$, and $`0`$ of its $`44`$ runs in
the dead band; across all $`220`$ runs the $`26`$ with twenty or more
novel writes have $`0`$ in the band and the $`161`$ with none have $`6`$
(Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ The premise is not uniformly true either, and our two arms disagree about what follows. ‣ 4.1.1 Two objections to the empty interval ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")(a)).
That log counts *writes* and not distinct values, which matters, because
a novel value once written is retrievable and can be reinforced.

E-real resolves the ambiguity and points the other way. Its planted
falsehood is *another real capital* rather than a one-digit corruption
(realfacts.py), its models produce novel errors at a pooled $`q`$ of
$`0.26`$, and it logs the number of distinct values in each retrieved
window. On the $`360`$ real-fact runs at $`f_{0}{=}0.9`$ the runs with
five or more novel writes carry a mean of $`2.51`$ distinct retrieved
values against $`1.66`$ for the rest, so their stores really did go
multi-valued, and they hold $`5`$ of $`41`$ runs in the dead band
against $`6`$ of $`311`$, a factor of $`6.4`$. Within granite-4.1-8b
alone it is $`4/39`$ against $`1/141`$. The registered criterion P-T1-N6
still passes, at $`0.014`$ overall against the synthetic control’s
$`0.125`$; what does not survive is the reading that a richer answer
space leaves the interval empty.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 5: What the empty interval needs, and what it does not. (a) Every
E-bimodal2 run by the number of novel-value *writes* it made; the log
counts writes, not distinct values. The three models that never scatter

being captured on $`44`$ of $`44`$ seeds with nothing in the dead band.
(b) Scripted controls, with the two measured points laid on them. The

which is why
§[4.1.1](#S4.SS1.SSS1 "4.1.1 Two objections to the empty interval ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
relocates the open question from count to distinguishability.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

#### 4.1.2 The arm bought to settle it

The question left open above is whether the empty interval needs the
store’s falsehoods to be few, or indistinguishable, or neither. It is
not answerable from data on disk, every arm this paper had planting
exactly one falsehood. It was therefore registered
(prereg/E_MULTIVALUE_PREREG.md), amended twice *before* any spend, and
run: three cells, twenty seeds, five models, $`300`$ runs, \$2.45
against a hard stop of \$7.30. Each cell plants three falsehoods
differing only in how far apart those three are: near uses the published
one-digit corruption three times over, far uses different magnitudes
plus a leading-digit change, and sem uses three different real capitals.
near against far is the load-bearing contrast and holds the world fixed;
sem changes the world too and is a bridge to
§[4.6](#S4.SS6 "4.6 The synthetic world on a real axis ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"),
which is that cell at one falsehood.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Two measurements explain the pair of nulls, and neither was predicted.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

What the arm does not settle is
§[4.1.1](#S4.SS1.SSS1 "4.1.1 Two objections to the empty interval ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")’s
disagreement; it narrows rather than closes it. sem lands at $`0.010`$,
beside
§[4.6](#S4.SS6 "4.6 The synthetic world on a real axis ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")’s
one-falsehood $`0.019`$ and away from far’s $`0.000`$, so the world
carries an effect distinguishability does not. E-real’s correlation is
not reverse causation either: the band occupancy of runs producing a
novel error in their *first three steps* is already $`4.0\times`$ that
of runs producing none, so it is present before the outcome is. Six of
the eleven real-fact runs in the band produce no novel error at all,
however, and with $`\gamma`$ measured blind to scattering no mechanism
is left on the table. Row 1k stays split with the count and the
distinguishability of planted falsehoods excluded, two candidates fewer
than before the money was spent.

#### 4.1.3 The cost of deciding the disagreement

The paragraph above reports two arms that disagree and declines to pick
one. That is honest and not a complete answer, because two different
questions are folded into the disagreement and only one is about sample
size. Both are answered here in arithmetic rather than adjectives, so a
reader pressing the point can see the number and check it
(Table [5](#S4.T5 "Table 5 ‣ 4.1.3 The cost of deciding the disagreement ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).

|  quantity | value |
|----|----|
|  difference in band occupancy, multi-valued minus two-valued | $`0.1027`$ |
|  unclustered standard error, and its $`z`$ | $`0.0517`$, $`z=1.99`$ |
|  clusters: Wikidata facts $`\times`$ runs each | $`36\times 10`$ |
|  fact-level $`\mathrm{ICC}`$, and the design effect it implies | $`0.077`$, $`1.69`$ |
|  $`95\%`$ interval, $`\sqrt{\mathrm{deff}}`$ rule of thumb | $`[-0.0292,\,0.2345]`$ spans $`0`$ |
|  $`95\%`$ interval, facts resampled with replacement | $`[0.0055,\,0.2412]`$ excludes $`0`$ |
|  bootstrap mass at or below $`0`$ | $`0.0201`$ |
|  runs per group for $`80\%`$ power, independent | $`97`$ |
|  …and with the measured design effect | $`164`$ |
|  multi-valued share of runs, so total runs needed | $`0.116`$, $`1405`$ |
|  …which is this many facts, against the corpus we have | $`\mathbf{141}`$ against $`36`$ |

Table 5: What it would cost to decide the within-arm half of the
disagreement, and what it already costs to state it honestly. Every row
is recomputed from results/ANSWERSPACE.json at build time. The two
intervals are the same contrast under two treatments of the same
clustering, and *they do not agree*: the rule of thumb spans zero and
the resampling does not.

##### Question one, within E-real, is decided, and only just, which is the part worth printing.

Runs whose store went multi-valued hold the dead band at $`0.1220`$
against $`0.0193`$ for the two-valued ones, a difference of $`0.1027`$.
The runs are *not* independent: the $`360`$ runs at $`f_{0}{=}0.9`$ sit
on $`36`$ Wikidata facts, ten runs each, and the fact-level intraclass
correlation is $`0.077`$, so the design effect is $`1.69`$ and any
interval computed as though the runs were independent is
anti-conservative. Two ways of accounting for that disagree, and we
report the one that is a measurement while naming the one that is a
rule. Scaling the standard error by $`\sqrt{\mathrm{deff}}`$, the
textbook correction, widens the interval to $`[-0.0292,\,0.2345]`$,
which spans zero. Resampling the $`36`$ *facts* with replacement,
$`20{,}000`$ draws, gives $`[0.0055,\,0.2412]`$, which does not, with
$`2.0\%`$ of the draws at or below zero. A design effect is a rule of
thumb applied to a variance; a cluster bootstrap is the sampling
distribution of the statistic actually computed, so the bootstrap
decides. We print both so a reader who applies the rule of thumb finds
the discrepancy here rather than in a review, and because $`2.0\%`$ is
not a comfortable margin: this contrast is decided at the edge of its
own resolution, and one more fact behaving like the two that carry most
of the band mass would undo it.

##### Question two, between the arms, is not a power question at all and no corpus size settles it.

E-bimodal2’s highest-scattering model has an *empty* band on $`44`$ of
$`44`$ seeds; E-real’s multi-valued subset has the *fullest* one. The
arms disagree not about a rate but about what a novel value *is*:
another variant of one numeral in the synthetic world, a different city
on the real axis. An item count cannot decide a construct difference,
which is why the arm this paper bought manipulated *distinguishability*
rather than buying more items, and why it returned the removal of two
candidate mechanisms rather than a verdict
(§[4.1.2](#S4.SS1.SSS2 "4.1.2 The arm bought to settle it ‣ 4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).
The criterion companion’s rule applies to us in the direction that costs
us: a criterion whose axis cannot express the difference under test is
not repaired by a larger $`n`$ \[[12](#bib.bib71)\].

##### The price of the replication that would decide question one.

At the observed rates, $`80\%`$ power at two-sided $`0.05`$ needs $`97`$
runs per group if the runs were independent and $`164`$ with the
measured design effect. Only $`0.116`$ of runs go multi-valued, and
multi-valuedness is an *outcome* rather than an assignment (we cannot
allocate to it), so reaching $`164`$ multi-valued runs takes about
$`1{,}405`$ runs in total, at ten runs per fact $`\mathbf{141}`$ real
facts against the $`\mathbf{36}`$ this paper has. That is a fourfold
corpus and not a re-analysis, which is the point of this subsection: the
external-validity objection to this paper is correct, it has a price,
and the price is written down where a reader can check the arithmetic
instead of asking for it.

Chosen by rule rather than picked: the lowest and highest
$`f_{\mathrm{end}}`$ among this model’s $`44`$ fresh seeds. $`j`$ is how

the seed selects the topic and the false value, and from there the

by lowest seed so the table is reproducible, and no run was chosen for

Two things in the bottom row are worth naming. First, neither run is

#### 4.1.6 What the limit says about the two outcomes

The mean-field equation
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
cannot produce two outcomes: it is deterministic and, when
$`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)<f`$, monotone, so $`f`$ decreases to zero
from any start. Four of five models satisfy
$`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f)<f`$ at $`f_{0}`$ and capture anyway, so the
bimodality lives in what
([1](#S3.E1 "In Definition 1 (The copy function). ‣ How 𝛾 is measured, and why it is not fitted. ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures"))
averages over, and the limit that motivates the apparatus says how much
room that leaves.

##### The derivation, and the bound it fails.

Writing the per-step change exactly and treating successive writes as
conditionally independent gives a *convergent* variance sum,
$`\sum_{n_{0}}^{N}\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(1-\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}})/n^{2}=O(1/n_{0})`$,
against a drift that grows like
$`(\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}{-}f)\ln(N/n_{0})`$: the noise a run can
accumulate over unbounded tenure is finite and set by how small the
store was at the start, so the spread of the limiting $`f`$ should fall
as $`1/\sqrt{n_{0}}`$ and the two outcomes should merge as the initial
store grows. Four sweeps at $`n_{0}\in\{10,20,40,80\}`$ refute it: an
eightfold increase should shrink the within-model spread by
$`\sqrt{8}=2.83`$ and it shrinks by $`1.07`$. What breaks is conditional
independence. Successive reads of the same store by the same model are
not independent draws from $`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}`$, and whatever
correlates them does not weaken as the store grows; the between-model
part stays flat, as a property of $`\gamma`$ rather than of $`n_{0}`$
should, which makes the failure interpretable rather than a
decomposition artefact
(Appendix [E](#A5 "Appendix E The variance bound under sweep ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).

The *drift* half stands and is what
§[4.3.1](#S4.SS3.SSS1 "4.3.1 Closed forms and a budget transient ‣ 4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
builds on. The *variance* half does not, so we claim no bound on the
outcome spread, and bimodality is measured at $`f_{0}\in\{0.1,0.9\}`$
and unexplained at the level of a mechanism. What is now known to be
missing is a model of the correlation between successive reads, a
sharper open problem than we had before the check.

##### Ordinal, and silent about location.

The per-model early copy rate orders the per-model capture rate at
Spearman $`+0.92`$ (window $`3`$) to $`+0.98`$ (window $`8`$–$`10`$),
stable across window widths. The mean-field sign criterion, capture iff
$`\gamma_{\mathrm{eff}}(f_{0})>f_{0}`$, does not locate the boundary:
four of five models drift downward at $`f_{0}`$ and capture one to two
runs in three anyway. Existence and ordering are measured; location is
not derived.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### 4.2 What a falling score measures

#### 4.2.1 Two boundaries, not two attractors

Before the control, one structural fact decides what the control can
find. At $`n_{0}{=}10`$, $`n_{\mathrm{false}}(0){=}9`$, $`R{=}0`$ and
$`150`$ steps,
Prop. [1](#Thmproposition1 "Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")’s
ceiling is $`159/160=0.9938`$. That proposition is elementary and the
single most useful result in this paper, for a reason unrelated to its
difficulty: $`f_{\max}(R)`$ moves with the budget, and
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Four interventions ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
records a frozen criterion of ours that failed for exactly that reason,
derivable from

Every quantity above is a single-draw score: retrieve $`k`$, ask once,
was the answer the truth. This apparatus conserves $`C`$ by
construction, which is why the control is interpretable: by
Prop. [1](#Thmproposition1 "Proposition 1 (Append-only ceiling). ‣ 3.1 Formal setting: three propositions ‣ 3 The synthetic apparatus ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
no truth record can leave an append-only store, so what the store can
answer is fixed and only the reader’s commitment moves. The control
measures a mismeasurement of known sign and needs no external
calibration
(Table [9](#S4.T9 "Table 9 ‣ 4.2.1 Two boundaries, not two attractors ‣ 4.2 What a falling score measures ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")).

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 8: What a falling score measures. Solid: single-draw accuracy,
which is what an exact-match score reads. Dashed: the truth appearing in
at least one of eight independent retrievals. The gap is what the store
still holds and the score does not report.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Two demarcations are owed. That exact match understates capability is
well known and usually attributed to *formatting* strictness, whereas
our two versions are semantically different answers; and that a single
pass rate conflates capability with reliability is the
pass@$`k`$/pass^(k) distinction, where unreliability is a property of
the agent to be measured. A third neighbour varies the scorer rather
than the system and finds the measurement moves with it
\[[70](#bib.bib37), [48](#bib.bib36), [50](#bib.bib32)\]; here the
scorer is fixed and exact, and what moves is $`s`$. What is new is a
setting in which $`C`$ is conserved by construction while $`s`$ moves,
which makes the gap a mismeasurement rather than a trade-off. The cost
to the rest of the paper is that claims phrased as capability loss must
be re-read as determinism loss; the dynamics of
§[4.1](#S4.SS1 "4.1 Bimodal outcomes, predicted by 𝛾 ‣ 4 Results ‣ Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself,and What a Falling Score Actually Measures")
are unaffected, $`f`$ being defined on the store’s contents and
$`\gamma`$ on the model’s reading.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### 4.3 Four interventions

Each intervention has its criteria in prereg/, committed before its data
existed, and is reported at whatever the criteria say. Two of the four
falsified a prediction of ours. The table comes first so a reader sees
what was at risk before what happened.

|  cost-matched state slot |  helps at low $`f_{0}`$, $`\geq 4/5`$; a direction at high $`f_{0}`$, $`\geq 4/5`$ same way |  our own two readings of what a self-fed slot does |  low supported; high a tie |
|  source marker |  harmless at low $`f_{0}`$; lowers capture at high $`f_{0}`$; lowers $`\gamma`$; each $`\geq 4/5`$ |  our own registered D13^(′) |  harmless supported; the other two failed |
